reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence and Cleanliness against all 30 Semantic Delta units and relevant committed implementation. Independent execution passed 428 tests across 25 files, including the real Neovim writeback round trip. Required workflow integration and output-contract behavior remain incomplete. HEAD remained unchanged throughout assessment.
findings: CRITICAL: Propose and Snack omit the required effective-diff review. src/core/templates/workflows/propose.ts:112-118 and src/core/templates/workflows/snack.ts:87-89 still invoke validate without --preview; default validation now returns no preview. The generated .pi/skills/xirang-propose/SKILL.md:159-162 and .pi/skills/xirang-snack/SKILL.md:137-139 inherit that omission. This violates the changed propose-workflow and snack-workflow Contracts requiring an explicitly requested preview and review before completion. `git grep -n -- '--preview' HEAD -- src/core/templates/workflows/propose.ts src/core/templates/workflows/snack.ts .pi/skills/xirang-propose/SKILL.md .pi/skills/xirang-snack/SKILL.md` returned no matches. scripts/measure-cli-context.mjs:43-53 repeats the omission, so its Propose comparison drops required review information from the new recipe. Update both workflows, verify the preview-review gate, and rerun the affected measurement.

CRITICAL: The replacement static guidance does not preserve the configuration-use contract. src/core/templates/fragments/artifact-references.ts:7-13 generates only Definition, artifact instruction and Template; src/core/templates/fragments/xirang-fragments.ts:204-208 supplies a shortened language rule. No shared guidance explains that context applies globally or that matching artifact rules add obligations without replacing built-in guidance, although config-projection explicitly requires those rules in shared skill/reference guidance. Propose and Snack query the data at src/core/templates/workflows/propose.ts:94-95 and src/core/templates/workflows/snack.ts:73-82, but querying data does not replace the omitted usage protocol. `git grep -n -E 'additive|rules\[artifactId\]|context.*all (applicable )?artifacts' HEAD -- src/core/templates .xirang/references .pi/skills` returned no matches. Restore one shared, discoverable configuration-use protocol and verify its delivery to applicable workflows.

CRITICAL: Bulk validation still emits progress in noninteractive calls. src/commands/validate.ts:43-56 computes interactivity but passes only explicit negated-option state to runBulkValidation; line 251 starts ora whenever --json and --no-interactive are absent. A source-level reproduction with XIRANG_INTERACTIVE=0 and `validate --changes` in a workspace containing no active changes returned exit 0, empty stdout, and stderr '- Validating...\n'. This violates the CLI and validation-commands Contracts requiring silent, problem-free noninteractive validation. Gate the spinner on actual interactivity and add coverage for default text execution without an explicit --no-interactive flag.

CRITICAL: An already-archived retry loses its required result. src/core/archive.ts:121-138 finds the existing archive path and then returns without emitting it. Reproducing `archive demo --json` with only .xirang/changes/archive/2026-01-01-demo present returned exit 0 with both streams empty. The changed change-archive Contract explicitly requires returning the existing archive location in this case. Emit that path using the same result representation as a newly completed archive and verify retry behavior.

CRITICAL: Explicit schema validation details disappear in JSON mode. src/commands/schema.ts:86-102 disables verbose stages when options.json is true and emits only issues. A reproduction of `schema validate semantic-model --verbose --json` returned exit 0 with both streams empty, despite the explicit detail request. The changed schema-commands Contract requires verbose check-stage details, and the design states that JSON controls encoding rather than removing explicitly requested content. Return structured details for this combination and test it.

CRITICAL: Existing JSON-format architecture invocations receive plain-text diagnostics. src/cli/index.ts:391-397 recognizes JSON mode only through the literal --json argument, while arch outline and snapshot retain --format json. Their error handlers use the shared diagnostic function at src/commands/arch/index.ts:101-104 and 125-128. Reproducing `arch outline --format json` without a model returned exit 1 and plain stderr 'Semantic Model unavailable: no Elements found\n'. Apply structured diagnostic encoding to the supported --format json invocation as well, including argument failures and warnings.

CRITICAL: Candidate text details omit the requested semantic diff. src/commands/candidate.ts:96-104 routes `candidate validate --details` through formatCandidateValidation, whose implementation at lines 52-67 prints only partition counts and 'Formal diff entries: N'. In an independently executed fixture changing the root Definition, text details showed only a count of one; the JSON form returned the actual root MODIFIED entry and before/after Definition. The changed deterministic-operations Contract requires details to return the real promotion diff, and the design requires checking information coverage separately for text and JSON. Render the requested diff in text mode and verify that changed identities and semantic content remain observable.

CRITICAL: Workflow navigation still mandates the higher-overhead JSON representation instead of implementing the approved reading policy. src/core/templates/fragments/xirang-fragments.ts:145-152 continues directing every consuming workflow to use JSON outline navigation and a full snapshot immediately after global context loss. The modified workflow-templates Contract instead requires markdown outline recovery, selected semantic reads, and snapshot only when necessary. The owner tests at test/core/templates/fragments/xirang-fragments.test.ts:235-269 still require the old JSON commands. Update the shared protocol and its generated consumers, and verify the intended navigation/recovery behavior rather than retaining assertions for the superseded policy.

CRITICAL: Feedback fallback retains expressly excluded output decoration, and its test still enforces that old behavior. src/commands/feedback.ts:164-171 invokes displayFormattedFeedback for text fallback; lines 113-119 emit the FORMATTED FEEDBACK and END FEEDBACK separators. test/commands/feedback.test.ts:390-416 explicitly requires those separators and passed during review. The modified feedback-command Contract requires complete manual-submission materials without decorative separators. Preserve the title, body, labels and URL while removing the decoration and updating the obsolete assertion.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change for completeness, correctness, coherence and cleanliness. Targeted verification passed 12 files / 156 tests, but three contract gaps remain: archive validation failures can exit successfully, Build does not request the Formal comparison it must present, and schema failure diagnostics omit the required package path. HEAD remained unchanged and the worktree remained clean.
findings: CRITICAL — Archive final-validation failure still produces a successful exit. src/core/archive.ts:268-272 prints compilation errors and returns false without throwing or setting process.exitCode; execute returns normally at src/core/archive.ts:143-148, so the CLI failure handler at src/cli/index.ts:195-201 never runs. A read-only probe of the validation gate with an unavailable model produced MISSING_PROJECT_ROOT, gateResult:false and exitCode:0. This violates the newly required failure semantics in .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/cli.md:102-113 and can cause an automation consumer to treat a rejected archive as completed. Make validation rejection propagate a nonzero exit while retaining the active Change, and cover that CLI failure path.

CRITICAL — Build loses the Formal comparison needed before promotion. src/commands/candidate.ts:97-106 now returns only reviewDigest unless --details is supplied. Every validation invocation in src/core/templates/workflows/build.ts:59-97 still omits --details, although step 13 explicitly requires presenting Formal comparison; the generated skill repeats this mismatch at .pi/skills/xirang-build/SKILL.md:132-135. The command `git grep -n 'candidate validate.*--details' HEAD -- src/core/templates/workflows/build.ts .pi/skills/xirang-build/SKILL.md test/core/templates/build.test.ts` returned no matches. The existing template tests inspect digest and ordering tokens but do not establish a route to comparison data. This violates the information-coverage requirement in .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/workflow-templates.md:93-99. Request comparison details at the final review/presentation point, update the generated surface, and verify that the workflow obtains either the actual Formal diff or the explicit unavailable reason.

CRITICAL — Schema validation failure diagnostics discard the required package location. validateBuiltInSchema retains the resolved schema directory in result.path at src/commands/schema.ts:31-62, but the failure output at src/commands/schema.ts:99-104 serializes only name and issues; text output also omits the package directory. Issue paths are merely schema.yaml or artifacts.<id>.template, so the response no longer identifies the installed package location that needs repair. The explicit target contract requires name, package path and concrete issues together in stderr (.xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/schema-commands.md:16-19). Preserve result.path in failure diagnostics and add coverage for an invalid built-in schema/template; the inspected tests at test/commands/schema.test.ts:40-60 exercise successful validation and verbose stages only.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change across Completeness, Correctness, Coherence and Cleanliness, including all six goals and Required Corrections. The selected 37 test suites passed (547 tests), but the CLI-wide output boundary remains incomplete for view and the instructions removal leaves an orphaned implementation of the retired enriched-response protocol. HEAD remained unchanged and the worktree was clean.
findings: CRITICAL — G1: view bypasses the required result/diagnostic boundary. src/cli/index.ts:392-400 adds and advertises --json on every leaf command, including view, but src/cli/index.ts:173-181 drops that option. src/core/view.ts:49-62 launches LikeC4 start, while src/commands/arch/runner.ts:86-102 only captures export output and inherits both streams for start and validate; the cache preparation also invokes validate at src/core/likec4/artifact-cache.ts:49-53. Reproduced through the built entry point with a temporary minimal valid model, XIRANG_INTERACTIVE=0, NO_COLOR=1 and XIRANG_TELEMETRY=0: `xirang view --json --port 61894` printed workspace/layout messages, `✓ Valid (4 files)`, HMR/build progress and a boxed service URL on stdout, and `No likec4 documents found in workspace` as plain text on stderr. The service reached its URL and was terminated after observation. This violates .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/cli.md:102-118 and the design decision covering necessary service addresses, JSON diagnostics and noninteractive progress. Preserve the actual service address as a result, propagate the requested encoding and route/suppress child output according to its responsibility; cover this non-export runner path with a behavior test.

CRITICAL — G5 / Cleanliness: removing the instructions command leaves its enriched-response implementation and obsolete protocol tests behind. src/core/artifact-graph/instruction-loader.ts:256-348 still loads templates and live output/dependency state, reads current project config, compiles configProjection and returns the combined instruction response; it remains re-exported at src/core/artifact-graph/index.ts:35-46. Its prompt-only chain remains at src/core/config-projection.ts:397-409. The new delivery uses artifactReferences at src/core/templates/fragments/artifact-references.ts:7-13, and the retired generator has no remaining production consumer: `rg -n '\b(generateInstructions|projectConfigForInstructions|projectConfigForPrompt)\b' src --glob '!config-projection.ts' --glob '!instruction-loader.ts' --glob '!index.ts' --glob '!**/completions/**'` returned no matches (exit 1). Nevertheless test/core/artifact-graph/instruction-loader.test.ts:170-183,493-542,789-811 still requires the removed combined response and its config/warning behavior. This is a half migration directly caused by the command removal, conflicts with the new instruction-loader Definition and removal of Template Enrichment (.xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/instruction-loader.md:8,19-25), and meets reviewer-cleanliness's CRITICAL orphan-code rule. Remove the retired response generator, its exclusive helpers/types/exports and obsolete assertions; preserve shared template/context/status loading and the required runtime configuration projection, and test those surviving consumers instead.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative baseCommit-to-HEAD Change across completeness, correctness, coherence, and cleanliness, including all 30 Element Delta units, the empty remaining Delta partitions, applicable Formal contracts, committed implementation, and owning tests. Two required output behaviors remain incorrect. Read-only execution confirmed the text-status regression; the feedback defect is established by implementation and its existing test. HEAD remained unchanged and the repository stayed clean. Full tests/build and cross-platform execution were not rerun in this review.
findings: CRITICAL: Text status drops required artifact paths. src/commands/workflow/status.ts:73-78 prints artifact identifiers and dependency gaps but never outputPath or the existing output paths collected at lines 23-29. Running the committed source with `TSX_DISABLE_CACHE=1 XIRANG_TELEMETRY=0 XIRANG_INTERACTIVE=0 node --import ./likec4/node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs src/cli/index.ts status --change reduce-cli-context-output` returned only `[x] proposal`, `[x] design`, `[x] specs`, and `[x] tasks`; its JSON counterpart retained the path patterns and 33 actual output paths. This violates the unchanged instruction-loader / Status Formatting requirement that each artifact show its output path pattern (.xirang/model/elements/instruction-loader.md:71-73), alongside the retained-path requirement in .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/artifact-workflow-commands.md:13-26. Restore the required paths in compact text output and protect this behavior in the owning status tests; current text assertions at test/commands/artifact-workflow.test.ts:162-190 and 214-220 only check counts, names, and indicators.

CRITICAL: Unauthenticated feedback fallback puts actionable authentication guidance on the wrong channel and loses it in JSON mode. src/commands/feedback.ts:162-169 emits only a generic authentication warning to stderr; `gh auth login` is printed to stdout exclusively in the non-JSON branch. The modified feedback contract explicitly requires both the authentication warning and concrete guidance on stderr, with manual-submission materials on stdout (.xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/feedback-command.md:28-32). Thus text consumers receive diagnostic advice in their result stream, while JSON consumers never receive the recovery instruction. Emit the authentication remedy through the diagnostic path in both modes and update test/commands/feedback.test.ts:117-148, which still asserts the obsolete stdout placement; the JSON fallback test at lines 152-157 covers only the missing-gh branch.

WARNING: Archive guidance still describes a removed success receipt. src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:159-160, also materialized in .pi/skills/xirang-archive-change/SKILL.md, says the CLI prints the Git handoff reminder. The final CLI returns only the archive location at src/core/archive.ts:137-140 and 161-165, as required by .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/change-archive.md:76-84. Update the generated guidance from its template source so consumers are not told to expect the retired reminder.

reviews.summary: Assessed Completeness, Correctness, Coherence and Cleanliness across the cumulative Change, including all 30 Semantic Delta units. Found two CRITICAL issues: Candidate provenance validation does not satisfy the retained Contract, and the Record filename migration leaves orphaned path-generation code and obsolete tests. TypeScript checking and the active-command-reference audit passed. HEAD remained unchanged and the checkout remained clean.
findings: CRITICAL — Correctness/Completeness: Candidate validation does not validate the format and source identity of record-source.md and record-coverage.json, as required by .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/candidate-commands.md:38-41. In src/core/candidate/validator.ts:193-217 these files receive layout and canonical-text checks; validateMetadata at lines 233-269 checks only candidate.yaml. Lines 272-280 include provenance bytes in the digest while parsing only partition files as semantics; lines 311-329 contain no provenance-format or source-identity validation. The owning test explicitly accepts coverage containing only {"schemaVersion":1}, without filename, source binding or entries, and accepts a changed coverage schemaVersion (test/commands/candidate-validate.test.ts:75-106). Such a Candidate can receive a usable digest from src/commands/candidate.ts:103-106 and satisfy promotion's validity/digest checks at src/core/candidate/promotion.ts:209-212. Validate the required provenance format and source binding without modifying the files or treating historical content as normative model input, and replace the permissive assertions with meaningful rejection coverage.

CRITICAL — Cleanliness: The Record filename migration removes the production callers of managedRecordFilename and managedRecordPath but leaves both old slug-plus-explorationId constructors in src/core/record/paths.ts:25-30, together with their obsolete path-construction test at test/core/record/paths.test.ts:17-23. Final workspace operations use validateRecordFilename and contained filename paths instead (src/core/record/workspace.ts:179-207,235-245). Search evidence: `rg -n 'managedRecord(Filename|Path)' src test` returned only the two definitions, their internal call, and the test import/call; there are no production consumers. Remove this orphaned construction chain and its retired-protocol assertion, preserving the current filename, containment and platform-path tests.

reviews.summary: Independently reviewed the cumulative Change across Completeness, Correctness, Coherence, and Cleanliness, including all 31 Element Delta units, committed implementation, relevant dependencies, and owning tests. Four remaining gaps prevent acceptance: completion helpers contaminate result output, global-config warnings bypass JSON diagnostics, current Quality status omits Opt commit associations, and generated Archive guidance contradicts the independent Sync gate. HEAD remained unchanged and the project worktree remained clean. Committed-source probes used in-memory filesystem boundaries; the build, full test suite, Windows checks, and Neovim checks were not rerun during this read-only review.
findings: CRITICAL — G1 / completion-command: the output boundary does not cover the real installers. src/commands/completion.ts:130-150 calls installer.install before emitting its JSON result, while src/core/completions/installers/fish-installer.ts:58-76 uses console.debug for the ordinary first-install ENOENT. Node sends console.debug to stdout, so completion install fish --json receives a plain-text line before the JSON result. The committed-source probe reproduced a successful first install with this unexpected stdout using only in-memory filesystem operations. The same path exists in zsh-installer.ts:258-279, bash-installer.ts:245, and powershell-installer.ts:314; PowerShell additionally emits unstructured warnings at powershell-installer.ts:191-216 and 248-277. Installer instruction arrays also retain success receipts (for example bash-installer.ts:314-329 and powershell-installer.ts:367-380), which the command now forwards unchanged. This violates elements/cli.md:104-118 and the completion output contract in the Change. Route actual helper diagnostics through the shared encoder, suppress ordinary missing-file debug output, and retain only necessary activation instructions. test/commands/completion.test.ts:11-29 mocks the installer completely, so its one-JSON-result assertion at lines 131-135 cannot detect this behavior; exercise a real installer with an isolated filesystem boundary.

CRITICAL — G1 / unified JSON diagnostics: src/core/global-config.ts:114-129 and 159-163 still write plain strings directly with console.warn/console.error. These are reachable through config list/get/set and other global-config consumers; src/commands/config.ts:78-85 reads getGlobalConfig before returning the requested JSON. With retired optimization fields, obsolete profile/workflows/delivery fields, or malformed config.json, --json therefore produces non-JSON stderr. Three committed-source probes confirmed these cases without writing files. The CLI diagnostic mode in src/cli/index.ts:392-402 cannot encode direct console calls, contrary to .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/cli.md:104 and design.md:29-35. Route global-config warnings through the common diagnostic boundary and verify valid result data plus structured stderr in JSON mode. The owning tests at test/core/global-config.test.ts:165-177 and 198-212 only assert string warnings and do not cover the new encoding contract.

CRITICAL — G2 / current Quality information is over-reduced: src/commands/quality.ts:72-80 projects a delivered Opt to only {disposition:'delivered'}, dropping every baseCommit/resultCommit association. The default query can report needs_optimize or all_done without identifying the delivered result commit; obtaining that current association requires loading the entire --history record. The approved decision explicitly requires default quality status to retain current Review/Opt/Seal conclusions and associated commits (.xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/design.md:55-59). These bindings also determine the next accepted Opt base in src/core/quality/engine.ts:235-247. Keep a compact current Opt commit association in the default projection while leaving opinion prose and historical records behind --history. test/commands/quality.test.ts:57-79 covers only not_performed and asserts state/history separation, so it does not establish the required delivered-Opt projection.

CRITICAL — G5 / Archive workflow coherence: src/core/templates/workflows/archive-change.ts:156-160 and its committed generated consumer .pi/skills/xirang-archive-change/SKILL.md:46-50 still state that archive performs Sync and tell the Agent not to duplicate sync writes. The actual CLI only checks pending Sync and throws with 'Run xirang sync ... first' (src/core/archive.ts:232-240); it does not apply the model. A sealed Change with pending Delta therefore follows the published steps into a deterministic failure, rather than completing Sync before archive. This contradicts the Change's preserved independent Sync/Archive boundary (.xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/change-archive.md:39-50 and elements/change-sync.md:21-31). Replace the stale instruction with an explicit conditional xirang sync step followed by archive, and keep the success summary accurate about which operation changed Formal. The owning runtime test already establishes rejection of pending Sync at test/core/archive.test.ts:220-225; generated-surface parity alone cannot establish agreement with that behavior.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the entire cumulative Change across Completeness, Correctness, Coherence and Cleanliness. Required warning preservation remains incomplete in Sync and Archive. The targeted suite passed 21 files / 261 tests, and TypeScript checking passed, but those results do not resolve the reproduced diagnostic loss. HEAD remained unchanged throughout the review.
findings: CRITICAL — G1: Sync and Archive discard successful compilation warnings. src/core/change-sync.ts:94-118 reads compiled.diagnostics only on failure and returns no warnings to src/commands/sync.ts:55-68; src/core/archive.ts:268-272 likewise returns success without emitting warnings when compiled.valid is true. Reproduced in both text and JSON modes using a valid project whose element-kind project unit is stored at model/views/project.md and a Change modifying the root definition: `validate --change sample [--json]` exits 0 and reports ENTITY_PARTITION_MISMATCH with views/project.md, but `sync sample --no-verify [--json]` changes Formal successfully with both streams empty. Subsequent `archive sample --yes --no-verify [--json]` returns the archive location and only the explicit bypass notice, omitting the same validation warning. The bypasses leave validation enabled. This violates .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/change-sync.md:80-82, elements/change-archive.md:76-80, elements/cli.md:102-118, and design.md:29-35, which require actual warnings/gate diagnostics to survive output reduction. Propagate successful compiler warnings to stderr through the command output boundary, encode them structurally with --json, and add regression coverage for successful Sync and Archive with warnings while preserving silence for problem-free operations.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the entire cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence and Cleanliness against the proposal, design, tasks, all 30 Semantic Delta units, selected Formal declarations/contracts and committed implementation. The focused suite passed 341 tests across 20 files, including the real Neovim CLI roundtrip. Independent source-executed probes nevertheless reproduced two remaining contract violations: List suppresses real compiler warnings, and text configuration projection loses multiline value boundaries. HEAD remained unchanged and the project working tree remained clean.
findings: CRITICAL — Preserve compiler warnings in List. src/core/list.ts:87-109 reads the Formal model and compiles each Change for --json/--long, but retains only title and deltaCount and drops the returned diagnostics. This violates the whole-CLI warning preservation requirement in .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/cli.md:102-118 and the design decision at design.md:29-35. Reproduced from committed source using a valid minimal model whose project Kind is stored in views/project.md: show sample --json returns valid data and ENTITY_PARTITION_MISMATCH on stderr, whereas list --json and list --long return their normal data with exit 0 and empty stderr for exactly the same Change. Route genuine compiler warnings to stderr with the requested encoding and useful Change/path attribution, without replacing the list result. Add a behavioral regression covering both list encodings and warning-free silence; the inspected List owner test/core/list.test.ts currently exercises ordinary results but does not detect this suppression.

CRITICAL — Preserve multiline scalar boundaries in text config projection. src/commands/config.ts:112-125 sends the selected nested configuration to formatValueYaml; src/core/config-schema.ts:302-324 inserts string values directly without multiline scalar framing or continuation indentation. A context value 'first line
rules: context content only
' and one proposal rule 'first rule
- still the same rule
' produce apparent top-level 'rules: context content only' and an unindented '- still the same rule', outside their original values. The equivalent --json query exactly preserves both values. This does not express the same nested configuration or keep a multiline rule as one rule, as required by .xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/config-command.md:86-96 and elements/config-projection.md:45-47. Use an unambiguous multiline text representation while retaining the original scalar contents and selected nesting. Extend the owning CLI tests with multiline context and a single multiline rule containing key/list-like text; the inspected test/commands/config.test.ts:164-191,274-292 verifies selection and simple text only, while test/core/project-config.test.ts:1089-1151 verifies loading rather than text delivery.

WARNING — The revised CLI documentation still contains a contradictory obsolete Quality overview. docs/cli.md:51-53 advertises allowed-next-operations, a nonexistent 'quality optimize' command, evidence-fingerprint matching to current code, and automatic checkpoint restoration, while its new Quality section at docs/cli.md:328-340 describes v4 commit-bound opinions, revision-only receipts and no workspace-freshness comparison. The actual registrations/results in src/commands/quality.ts:17-81 agree with the new section. Update the overview so readers receive one consistent protocol; the same documentation diff also removes the archive command reference without a replacement, leaving only the summary-table entry and workflow material elsewhere. This is a documentation coherence risk rather than an additional runtime blocker.

reviews.summary: Independently assessed the entire cumulative Change for Completeness, Correctness, Coherence and Cleanliness. The main output, status, Quality, Record, Candidate, workflow and Neovim paths are supported by inspection and 458 passing tests across 26 suites, plus eight passing Neovim headless modes. Three corrections remain: silent setup configuration failures, ambiguous single-line configuration scalars, and a newly dead import. Normal typechecking, the active-command reference audit and cumulative diff whitespace checks passed. HEAD remained unchanged and the repository worktree stayed clean.
findings: CRITICAL — Correctness/Completeness: setup can silently succeed after failing to create its project configuration. src/core/setup.ts:582-587 catches every config.yaml write error and returns 'skipped'; the rewritten result handling at src/core/setup.ts:595-617 ignores configStatus and the underlying error. Consequently the CLI action at src/cli/index.ts:119-130 receives no exception and has no failure to report. A probe executing the committed SetupCommand with tools='none', interactive=false and an injected EACCES only for config.yaml resolved successfully with configExists=false, stdout=[] and stderr=[]. This violates G1 and workspace-init's Setup output messaging (.xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/workspace-init.md:17-19), which preserve real failures and actual workspace creation duties, and cli's failure semantics (elements/cli.md:102-104). Preserve the original write error and path and report it through the diagnostic/failure channel; add an owning regression that fails configuration creation after other setup writes succeed.

CRITICAL — Correctness/Coherence: the compact configuration text remains ambiguous for valid single-line context and rules. src/core/config-schema.ts:303-306 serializes strings safely only when they contain a newline, while src/commands/config.ts:125 uses that formatter for the selected nested configuration. With context='Use # Root as a heading' and proposal rules ['- Required rollback plan', 'Include: rollback plan'], the actual CLI exits 0 with empty stderr but emits 'context: Use # Root as a heading', '- - Required rollback plan' and '- Include: rollback plan'. Parsing that YAML-like mapping yields context='Use', a nested sequence and a mapping, whereas --json preserves the full context and two strings. This loses the scalar/rule boundaries promised by config-command's project-query contract (.xirang/changes/reduce-cli-context-output/elements/config-command.md:90-96). The existing parity test at test/commands/config.test.ts:178-195 covers multiline strings only. Quote or serialize special single-line scalars as well, and extend parity coverage to Markdown comments, list/mapping-looking strings, implicit booleans and empty context.

CRITICAL — Cleanliness: src/core/setup.ts:10 retains an unused chalk import after this Change removes all its consumers from the success renderer. 'git grep -n chalk HEAD -- src/core/setup.ts' returns only the import, whereas the same search at baseCommit a01cacf4e2f43eec812bee588085749c3e0c359a returns the import and its former rendering uses. The stricter diagnostic check 'pnpm exec tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals --noUnusedParameters' confirms TS6133 at setup.ts:10; its other historical unused-code diagnostics are not findings here. Remove this newly dead import. Severity follows the explicit dead-import rule in .xirang/model/elements/reviewer-cleanliness.md:12-14; this is a small cleanup, not an assertion of a runtime failure.

reviews.summary: Reviewed the cumulative Change across Completeness, Correctness, Coherence and Cleanliness. Two reproducible contract violations remain in configuration output and auxiliary-command diagnostic routing. Focused verification passed 48 test files / 689 tests, TypeScript checking, lint and eight Neovim headless modes. HEAD remained unchanged and the checkout remained clean.
findings: CRITICAL — Full text configuration queries manufacture null values for absent optional fields. src/core/config-projection.ts:119-146 creates properties whose values are undefined; src/commands/config.ts:112-125 passes that object directly to the text renderer, and src/core/config-schema.ts:292-325 serializes undefined as null. Reproduced using a project whose .xirang/config.yaml contains only `schema: semantic-model`: `xirang config project` prints `proseLanguage: null`, `context: null`, `optimization: null` and `apply: null`, while `xirang config project --json` omits those fields.
